harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured zram-backed compressed swap on node1 (Ubuntu 24.04) via systemd's native zram-generator: installed systemd-zram-generator and the missing linux-modules-extra-6.8.0-71-generic package (zram kernel module was absent from the base image), set /etc/systemd/zram-generator.conf to zram-size = max(ram/2, 512) with zstd compression and swap-priority 100, and activated it. Result is a ~983.5 MB zstd-compressed zram0 swap device, exceeding the 512 MB minimum, with no disk-backed swap present so it is trivially the preferred (and only) swap. Verified the configuration is boot-persistent by rebooting node1 and confirming the swap reappeared automatically with no manual step, plus confirmed a genuine restart via changed boot_id/uptime.
actions_performed: Captured baseline: no existing swap on node1 (Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS, kernel 6.8.0-71-generic)
Installed systemd-zram-generator package
Wrote /etc/systemd/zram-generator.conf: zram0 with zram-size=max(ram/2,512), compression-algorithm=zstd, swap-priority=100, fs-type=swap
Diagnosed activation failure: zram kernel module missing from /lib/modules (modprobe zram failed)
Installed linux-modules-extra-6.8.0-71-generic to provide the zram module; loaded it with modprobe
Reset failed systemd units, reloaded systemd, started systemd-zram-setup@zram0.service
Verified 983.5MB zstd-compressed zram0 swap active at priority 100 via swapon --show, /proc/swaps, zramctl, free -h
Captured pre-restart boot_id baseline
Issued sudo systemctl reboot on node1, acknowledgement returned before disconnect
Polled node1 until exec succeeded again
Confirmed changed boot_id and new uptime -s timestamp, proving an actual restart occurred
Verified post-restart zram swap automatically active again (983.5MB, zstd, priority 100) with no manual reactivation, confirming boot persistence

evidence.requirement: At least 512MB compressed in-memory swap active and configured, preferred over disk-backed swap
evidence.summary: zram0 zstd-compressed device of 983.5MB (>512MB min) active as swap with priority 100; no disk-backed swap exists on the node so zram is the sole/highest-priority swap

Pre-restart baseline boot_id cf34dc87... captured with swap active; systemctl reboot acknowledged; node polled back online; new boot_id 0f182c01... (proving genuine restart) with zram0 swap automatically active again at 983.5MB/zstd/priority 100 with no manual re-activation
